minutes.headline: Parks Commission backed a Boys and Girls Club polar plunge and approved its park naming policy.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the Parks and Recreation director report on the summer town beach season, passes, programs and swim lessons. It also heard the facilities director on beach erosion, the beach house work and ideas for fall events. It voted to support a polar plunge fundraiser, approved the naming policy after adding a maintenance factor, and adjourned. Chair updates covered the Marshall Park state grant visit, a member's resignation and next steps for grants.

budget_items.topic: Town beach pass sales and scans
budget_items.what_was_said: Season scans and unique visitors were compared with passes sold. Day pass sales went through a separate point-of-sale system.

budget_items.topic: Summer programs, swim lessons and memberships revenue and profit
budget_items.what_was_said: The director reported total revenue and profit for the programs, swim lessons and memberships. Two programs did not cover costs; beach costs were not counted.
A member asked whether the town-side lifeguard line was over-expended. The answer was that it was slightly under, with the shortfall expected to be covered by the swim lesson revolving account.
figures_as_heard: a thousand two hundred dollars under

budget_items.topic: Revolving fund for swim lesson profit
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked that swim lesson profit go to the revolving account to cover lifeguard costs and not other lines. The director said registrations feed the revolving account automatically.

budget_items.topic: Polar plunge fundraising and town finances
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said money coming through the town must be budget related. She suggested another organization run the fundraising so it stays off town finances.

budget_items.topic: Beach house wall and floor materials
budget_items.what_was_said: Materials for walls, floors, trim and paint were estimated, assuming volunteer labor. Prevailing wage labor would be the biggest cost.

budget_items.topic: Using beach profit for beach house work
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair suggested using the beach and program profit for the beach house materials.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park funding plan and estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: A state visitor asked how the project would be funded, and ARPA funds were mentioned. Platforms on the trail and more fill for the parking lot and ball diamond could raise the estimate, though it was said to be on target overall.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park grants and engineering phase
budget_items.what_was_said: The next engineering phase is funded and a request for bids or qualifications would be drafted. The next big grant is the land and water conservation fund, due in January.
Green Communities helps upgrade existing items, not new construction. Utility rebates may be available if they are consulted before equipment is chosen.

decisions.decision: The Parks director will work with the Boys and Girls Club director on a plan for a polar plunge. Fire and police are to be consulted on timing, and the facilities director asked for as much notice as possible.
The Parks director expects to launch fall programs in about two weeks, planning to keep the school gym on Wednesdays.
A member will email the Boy Scout troop about sanding and repainting the town beach benches.
The Parks director agreed to look into a fall movie night at Marshall Park, including pricing, rights and Board of Health requirements.
The beach house will not be winterized yet so volunteer work days can be planned for the fall. The chair will coordinate volunteers.
The naming policy will be posted on the Parks page of the town website, and the chair will find who updates the site.
The next meeting is set for September 20th, on Zoom.
The vice chair will email the facilities director about protecting the new table.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to support a Boys and Girls Club polar plunge fundraiser and to work with Parks on it; the roll call was not clearly counted in the minutes.
The commission approved the parks naming policy as written, with added wording on ongoing maintenance in the location section; the roll call recorded three ayes.
The Parks director reported on beach passes, scans, programs, swim lessons and revenue; a member asked about the lifeguard line, which was reported slightly under budget.
The beach house will not be winterized yet, so volunteer work days can be planned for the fall, and the chair will coordinate volunteers.
The next engineering phase for Marshall Park is funded; the next large grant, from the land and water conservation fund, is due in January.

why_it_matters: The polar plunge and swim lesson discussions turned on keeping fundraising off town finances and sending swim lesson profit to the revolving account that covers lifeguards, which bears on who pays for beach staffing.
The naming policy, once posted on the town website, sets how parks are named, and the Marshall Park grant path determines how much outside money, rather than local tax money, may fund the project.
watch_next: The land and water conservation fund grant application for Marshall Park, due in January.
